### RenderTargetOptions

*interface*

Since API\_MINOR 8: `RenderTarget`'s options (three.js's; others are ignored).

```ts
export interface RenderTargetOptions { … }
```

- `count?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (`MRT_MINOR`; ignored before, and by `RenderTarget` and the array and 3D targets): a `WebGLRenderTarget`'s textures (three.js r185's multiple render targets; default 1). See `WebGLRenderTarget`.

- `depthTexture?: DepthTexture | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 35: its depth as a texture (`DepthTexture`), which makes `depthBuffer` true.

- `type?: number;`

  `UnsignedByteType` (default): RGBA8 holding what the window would show (tone mapped, sRGB-encoded). `HalfFloatType` (or `FloatType`, taken as half floats before API\_MINOR 34): linear light, not tone mapped, past 1 where it is. Before API\_MINOR 45 its passes clamp what they write to 0–65504 (negative and non-finite values 0, alpha 1 unless blended), a custom material's fragment too, so a signed value such as a distance field loses its negative half. Since API\_MINOR 45 (`HALF_FLOAT_UNCLAMPED_MINOR`) passes write it as three.js does, as they write a `FloatType` target: a custom material's fragment as it is (negative values, values past 1 and alpha included, without fog), built-in materials' light unclamped, blended as before, on every backend and with or without `generateMipmaps`; RGBA16F holds it to half-float precision (past ±65504 is ±infinity). This is the game's own targets: those the engine's modules make for themselves (the sky, weather, water and volumes) keep the clamped output, so they draw as at 44. Where the device cannot render half floats it holds RGBA8 at every minor (a warning says so), written as an `UnsignedByteType` target is (tone mapped, sRGB-encoded, clamped to 0–1: negative values are 0 there too) and, since API\_MINOR 10, counts RGBA8's 4 bytes a pixel against the image budget (8 before). Built-in maps read either as sRGB-encoded images; custom materials' programs read the values as they are.

  Since API\_MINOR 34 (`FLOAT_TARGETS_MINOR`) `FloatType` holds 32-bit floats, as three.js's (RGBA32F, and with `format` RG32F or R32F: 16, 8 and 4 bytes a pixel), for data passes such as an FFT's ping-pong: passes write their color as it is (a custom material's fragment unclamped, negative values and alpha included, without fog, as three.js's ShaderMaterial; built-in materials' light unclamped), unblended on every device (a blended material's color replaces what is there: WebGPU blends no 32-bit floats, nor does OpenGL ES without `EXT_float_blend`), and `textureLoad` reads exact values. Where the device does not filter them linearly (`renderer.capabilities .floatFilterable` false) they sample nearest whatever the filters say. Where it does not render them (`floatRenderable` false: OpenGL ES without `EXT_color_buffer_float`, WebGPU without `float32-filterable`) the target holds the half floats of as many channels, still written unclamped (blended materials blend there), counting their bytes. With `generateMipmaps` an RGBA `FloatType` target holds RGBA16F on every device, written unclamped the same way (its mip chain made from that), and a `FloatType` DataTexture still holds half floats.

- `wrapS?: Wrapping;`

  The texture's sampling (default clamped and linear).

- `wrapT?: Wrapping;`
- `magFilter?: MagnificationFilter;`
- `minFilter?: MinificationFilter;`

- `generateMipmaps?: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 9: a full mip chain of the color (a third more of the image budget), made again from the full-size image after each pass into the target (a downsampling pass on Direct3D 12 and WebGPU, `glGenerateMipmap` on OpenGL ES and WebGL2, blits on Vulkan, Metal's mipmap generation on macOS), which a mipmap `minFilter` samples (the default with it: `"linear-mipmap-linear"`). Default false: before API\_MINOR 9 it had to be false, and without it a mipmap filter samples the full-size image.

- `depthBuffer?: boolean;`

  Default true. Since API\_MINOR 9 false makes a target without a depth buffer (no depth counts against the image budget): its passes draw in order without depth tests, as three.js's (2D work: decals, scars, prints, minimaps of flat shapes).

- `format?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 10, with `HalfFloatType`: `RGFormat` holds two channels (red and green, RG16F: four bytes a pixel, half of RGBA16F's budget) and `RedFormat` one (R16F: two bytes); materials sampling them read blue 0 and alpha 1, and blending writes the channels the target has. Neither takes `generateMipmaps` (TypeError). Since API\_MINOR 11, with `UnsignedByteType` (the default type), `RGFormat` is RG8 (two bytes a pixel) and `RedFormat` R8 (one byte): marks and masks (soil and burn in RG8 plus depth in R8 take 3 bytes a pixel where RGBA8 takes 4). They hold what an RGBA8 target holds in those channels (the output as the window would show it, so a value meant as data is written sRGB-decoded, `srgb_to_linear`), clamped to 0–1 by every blend equation (additive past 1 stops at 1, reverse subtract below 0 at 0), read with blue 0 (and green 0 for R8) and alpha 1, take no mipmaps, render on every device and so never fall back, counting 2 and 1 bytes a pixel against the image budget from the start (before API\_MINOR 11 `UnsignedByteType` with these formats was a TypeError). Where half floats do not render (OpenGL ES without `EXT_color_buffer_float` or `EXT_color_buffer_half_float`) RG16F and R16F hold RGBA8 with a warning, as RGBA16F targets do, and count its 4 bytes a pixel. Targets made before the game's first frame (the runtime may not know the device yet) count the larger of the two (R16F 4 bytes), and are counted again at the first frame. Other formats hold RGBA, as before.

- `colorSpace?: string;`

### RenderTarget

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 8: an image the game draws scenes into (three.js `RenderTarget`/`WebGLRenderTarget`), for build icons rendered once, decals accumulated over time, mirrors and minimaps. `texture` is a `Texture` like any other: a material's `map` (or any built-in map), a custom material's texture uniform, `draw.image` and UI images; its rows are the top of the rendered image first, so a plane's UVs show it the right way up, as in three.js. It starts transparent black and keeps what passes draw into it until they draw over it or the target is resized (cleared again) or disposed; a lost and recovered GPU device clears it too. Width and height are 1 to 4,096 (RangeError); a game holds at most 16 (32 since API\_MINOR 35, `RENDER_TARGETS_32_MINOR`; RangeError), each counting its color and depth (four bytes a pixel each; half-float color eight, RG16F four and R16F two where half floats render, else four) against the image budget (`engine.budgets()`): a target of 4,096 pixels a side takes 128 MiB, so one covering a whole map needs the budget raised (`engine.limits.image_mib=300` in the manifest, since API\_MINOR 9). A target past the budget throws a RangeError saying so. Colors are premultiplied by alpha where blending made them partly transparent, as three.js leaves them: show a target with transparent edges with `premultipliedAlpha` materials. Since API\_MINOR 35 the game may read a target back asynchronously (`renderer.readRenderTargetPixelsAsync`).

```

- `readonly texture: Texture;`
- `readonly width: number;`
- `readonly height: number;`

- `readonly depthBuffer: boolean;`

  Whether passes into it depth-test (`RenderTargetOptions`).

- `depthTexture: DepthTexture | null;`

Setting one (or another, or null) after the target was made makes it again, cleared, its depth buffer the texture's; `dispose()` disposes it with the target.

### WebGLRenderTarget

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 8: three.js's name for `RenderTarget`.

Since API\_MINOR 38 (`MRT_MINOR`) it takes three.js r185's `count` (multiple render targets, a G-buffer): `count` textures, `textures[0]` being `texture` and each other a clone of its settings at construction (three.js's), of its size, format and type, without depth of their own. A pass into the target draws into all of them: a `ShaderMaterial` whose `fragmentShader` returns a struct of `@location(n)` `vec4f` members (location 0 among them, three.js's `pc_fragColor`) writes texture `n` from member `n`: location 0 as a `vec4f` fragment's color is written (fogged, tone mapped and encoded as the target's type says), the others as given (clamped to 0–1 in 8-bit textures). Built-in materials, and programs without a location, leave those textures as they are, as three.js's WebGLRenderer does with draw buffers a shader has no output for; a clear clears them all; blending applies to each alike (unblended where 32-bit floats). `renderer.readRenderTargetPixelsAsync` reads any by its `textureIndex`; `setSize`, a new `depthTexture` and `dispose()` take them all along. `count` is a whole number from 1 to 8 (RangeError), at most `renderer.capabilities.maxColorAttachments` here, and a sample of all the textures may take at most 32 bytes on every device (WebGPU's default `maxColorAttachmentBytesPerSample`, held natively too so a game draws the same targets everywhere), counted as WebGPU counts them: RGBA8 and RGBA16F 8 bytes, RGBA32F 16, RG8 2, R8 1, RG16F 4, R16F 2, RG32F 8, R32F 4 — so 4 × RGBA8 or HalfFloatType, or 2 × FloatType, fit, and past them the RangeError gives the arithmetic. Each texture counts as a render target (of the 32 a game holds) and against the image budget. MSAA is not offered with `count` past 1: `samples` above 0 with it is a RangeError (the engine's render targets are not multisampled, and `samples` is otherwise ignored). Older games' targets ignore `count`.

```ts
export class WebGLRenderTarget extends RenderTarget { … }
```

- `readonly isWebGLRenderTarget: true;`

- `readonly textures?: Texture[];`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (`MRT_MINOR`; absent before): its textures, `texture` first (one but with `count`).

### DepthTexture

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 35 (`DEPTH_TEXTURES_MINOR`; a TypeError before): three.js r185's `DepthTexture`, a render target's depth as a texture, given as its `depthTexture` (or the option) before or after it is made. After passes into the target it holds the depth they left: 0 at the camera's near plane to 1 at its far one (as three.js reads `gl_FragCoord.z`; linear in view depth under an orthographic camera), rows as the target's color, so the same `uv` reads both. A custom material's (`ShaderMaterial` or hooks) texture uniform holding one is, in its WGSL:

```text
NAME: texture_depth_2d, NAME_sampler: sampler
  (`textureSampleLevel(NAME, NAME_sampler, uv, 0)` gives the depth,
  an f32; nearest whatever its filters say: WebGPU binds depth to
  non-filtering samplers alone), or with
  `compareFunction` set
NAME: texture_depth_2d, NAME_sampler: sampler_comparison
  (`textureSampleCompare(NAME, NAME_sampler, uv, reference)` in a
  fragment, `textureSampleCompareLevel` anywhere: 1 where
  `reference compareFunction storedDepth` holds, else 0; with
  `LinearFilter` the four nearest texels' results blended
  bilinearly, a shadow map's percentage-closer filter, where the
  device filters it).
```

A material binds depth textures among its first five textures (the engine orders them first). A draw whose depth texture's target is gone draws nothing, and a pass cannot sample the depth of the target it draws into (it draws without it). Built-in materials' maps and `draw.image` show nothing for one. It counts with its target (the target's depth, 4 bytes a pixel, against the image budget; no further image). Natively Vulkan samples a target's depth in place, OpenGL ES a DEPTH\_COMPONENT24 texture, Direct3D 12 a typeless depth's R32 or R24 view and Metal its Depth32Float texture; in browsers WebGPU a depth24plus one.

```ts

```

      width: number,
      height: number,
      type?: number,
      mapping?: number,
      wrapS?: string,
      wrapT?: string,
      magFilter?: string,
      minFilter?: string,
      anisotropy?: number,
      format?: number,
    );
  ```

- `readonly isDepthTexture: true;`

- `compareFunction: number | null;`

  `LessEqualCompare` and the others, or null (default): no comparison.

- `type: number;`

  three.js's (default `UnsignedIntType`, `DepthFormat`).

- `format: number;`

### WebGLArrayRenderTarget

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 34 (a TypeError before): three.js's `WebGLArrayRenderTarget`, `depth` layers of `width × height` (a water's FFT cascades, a shadow's slices). The engine keeps them stacked top to bottom in one image of `width × height·depth`, so `height × depth` is at most 4,096 (RangeError), and the image counts against the budget as a target of that size. Its `texture` is a `texture_2d_array<f32>` of `depth` layers in a `ShaderMaterial`'s WGSL, as a `DataArrayTexture` is (`textureSample(t, t_sampler, uv, layer)`, `textureLoad(t, coords, layer, 0)`, `textureNumLayers`); built-in maps and `draw.image` show the whole stack. `height` and `viewport` are a layer's; `renderer.setRenderTarget(target, layer)` draws into one layer (three.js's `activeCubeFace`; RangeError past the last), and a pass may draw every layer at once through `renderer.setViewport(0, 0, width, height * depth)` after it (layer `l` is the rows from `l × height` down from the top, as `f.coord.y` counts them).

```ts
export class WebGLArrayRenderTarget extends RenderTarget { … }
```

- `constructor(width?: number, height?: number, depth?: number, options?: RenderTargetOptions);`
- `readonly isWebGLArrayRenderTarget: true;`
- `readonly depth: number;`

### WebGL3DRenderTarget

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 35 (`VOLUME_TEXTURES_MINOR`; a TypeError before): three.js r185's `WebGL3DRenderTarget`, `depth` slices of `width × height` whose `texture` is a Data3DTexture (a `texture_3d<f32>` in a ShaderMaterial's WGSL; zeros at first), for simulations kept in 3D (smoke, fire, clouds). `renderer.setRenderTarget(target, layer)` picks the slice `render` and `clear` draw into (three.js's `activeCubeFace`; RangeError past the last): each pass draws into the target's own 2D image (with its depth buffer unless `depthBuffer: false`), which is then copied into that slice on the GPU, in order with the passes around it, on every backend. `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync` reads that 2D image, the slice last drawn (three.js reads the layer last attached; `activeCubeFaceIndex` is not a 3D target's). UnsignedByteType with RGBAFormat or RedFormat, HalfFloatType with RGBAFormat, RGFormat or RedFormat, FloatType with RedFormat (other formats are a TypeError); no mipmaps or depthTexture. Sides 1 to 2,048 (RangeError past them; 256 on every device, past what one holds the 3D texture fails as an image does). Its 2D image and its 3D texture count as two images, each of its own bytes, and go together. `setSize(width, height, depth)` makes both again, cleared.

```ts
export class WebGL3DRenderTarget extends RenderTarget { … }
```

- `constructor(width?: number, height?: number, depth?: number, options?: RenderTargetOptions);`
- `readonly isWebGL3DRenderTarget: true;`
- `readonly texture: Data3DTexture;`
- `readonly depth: number;`
- `setSize(width: number, height: number, depth?: number): void;`

### TextureLoader

*class*

Loads package images (PNG or WebP; an animated WebP's first frame; since API\_MINOR 43, `JPEG_IMAGES_MINOR`, JPEG too: `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.jpe` and `.jfif`, baseline or progressive, turned by their Exif orientation as browsers show them) through the engine's decoders. Loads requested at once read their files side by side, each holding its file's size of the 64 MiB the engine keeps for files being read; past that they wait for the ones before them rather than fail. Their decoded pixels count against the engine's decoded-asset budget (64 MiB unless the player changed it) until each becomes a texture: at most 8 decode at once and the rest wait their turn, and a load that finds the budget full of the others' images waits for one of them and decodes again, so loads requested together never fail the budget (until host API 1.25 they failed with an EncodingError "asset budget exceeded").

```ts
export class TextureLoader { … }
```

- `constructor();`

- `loadAsync(path: string): Promise<Texture>;`

  Rejects with a TypeError for a bad path, an Error named `NotFoundError` for a missing file and `EncodingError` for an image it cannot decode; RangeError past the texture budget, with 128 loads already waiting (thrown by `loadAsync` itself), or for one image whose decoded pixels alone pass the decoded-asset budget (the message names its size, the budget and what images in use hold).

- `load(path: string, onLoad?: (texture: Texture) => void, onProgress?: unknown, onError?: (error: Error) => void): Texture;`

  From API\_MINOR 20 three.js's `load(url, onLoad, onProgress, onError)` (`onProgress` is never called). Games declaring an older minor pass `onError` third: `load(path, onLoad, onError)`.

  Since API\_MINOR 40 both also load `.ktx2` files of BC blocks, as `KTX2Loader` does (an engine extension), and a PNG or WebP image for which `starhermit package` made a KTX2 file (`engine.textures.compress`, the image's path with `.ktx2` added) loads that file in its place, or the image itself where that file fails to load. Images `engine.textures.exact` names get no KTX2 file and load byte for byte.

### GLTF

*interface*

What `GLTFLoader` gives: the default scene and every scene, as groups of the document's nodes.

```ts
export interface GLTF { … }
```

- `scene: Group;`
- `scenes: Group[];`

- `animations: AnimationClip[];`

  The model's animations as three.js's GLTFLoader makes them (since API\_MINOR 25: a clip an animation, a track a channel named by its node, CUBICSPLINE sampled as glTF's splines); empty before. From API\_MINOR 25 a skinned node's meshes are SkinnedMeshes bound to a Skeleton of its joints (Bones), and node and mesh names are three.js's (sanitized for track paths and made unique).

- `ignored: string[];`

  What the file has that was not applied, each once (extensions, texture transforms, maps on a second UV set, extra attributes, animations and skins, morph targets, images that did not decode), as the console warning names them.

### GLTFLoader

*class*

three.js's GLTFLoader for package `.glb` and `.gltf` files, read off the game's thread (since API\_MINOR 5). Each node becomes an `Object3D` with the node's name and transform: a `Mesh` for a mesh of one primitive, otherwise a `Group` holding a `Mesh` per primitive (the mesh's name on each). Materials are `MeshStandardMaterial` or `MeshBasicMaterial` for `KHR_materials_unlit` (base color only), with glTF 2.0's core material as three.js's GLTFLoader maps it: base color factor and `map`; metalness and roughness factors and the metallic-roughness texture as both `roughnessMap` and `metalnessMap`; `normalMap` with `normalScale` (scale, scale) (three.js negates y for glTF's unflipped UVs; the engine's are flipped, so it does not); `aoMap` with `aoMapIntensity` from the occlusion strength; `emissive`, `emissiveMap` and `emissiveIntensity` from `emissiveFactor` and `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`; alpha mode and cutoff; double-sided. Maps use UV set 0 only (the engine has no second UV set): one on `texCoord` 1 is left out. A primitive with `COLOR_0` gets its own copy with `vertexColors` (a four-component `color` attribute). Geometries carry `position`, `normal`, `uv` (in three.js's bottom-left convention) and 32-bit indices; a mesh used by several nodes shares its geometries. Draco-compressed primitives (`KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, as Blender and gltf-transform export them) and quantized attributes (`KHR_mesh_quantization`: 8- and 16-bit positions, normals and texture coordinates) are decoded in-house on the same thread; decoded Draco data counts toward the 128 MiB of binary data a document may hold. External buffers and images are package files beside the document (`uri` relative to it). Textures are made as three.js's GLTFLoader makes them: the glTF sampler's `magFilter`, `minFilter`, `wrapS` and `wrapT` (WebGL's codes as three.js's filter and wrapping constants; without a sampler, or for a filter it leaves unset, repeat wrapping, `LinearFilter` and `LinearMipmapLinearFilter`, with mipmaps for a mipmap minification filter), `SRGBColorSpace` for base color, and the texture's or image's name. glTF's top-left UVs are converted instead of setting three.js's `flipY = false` (the engine's textures have no `flipY`; the result looks the same). External and embedded PNG and WebP images (at most 16 MiB encoded) decode off the game's thread as textures, not canvases, so the canvas bounds do not apply: an image past 4,096 pixels on a side, or past what the game's image budget has left (`engine.limits.image_mib`; a 4096 × 4096 image with mipmaps takes 85 MiB of the default 56), is halved until it fits, as three.js and browsers resize a texture past the GPU's largest, with a console warning naming the image and the limit; one past the decoders' bounds (16,384 pixels on a side, 16,777,216 in all) or with no image budget left rejects the load with a RangeError naming the image and the limit. JPEG images (baseline and progressive) decode the same way since API\_MINOR 43 (`JPEG_IMAGES_MINOR`), their Exif orientation applied as `createImageBitmap` applies it, pixels as libjpeg-turbo decodes them; below 43 they are not decoded (the engine decodes PNG and WebP only); one, or an image that fails to decode or is missing, leaves its maps out. `EXT_texture_webp`, required or optional, is read as three.js reads it: the texture's WebP image first, its core `source` when that fails (named in the warning). `KHR_lights_punctual` (since API\_MINOR 22) makes lights as three.js r185's GLTFLoader does: a `DirectionalLight`, `PointLight` or `SpotLight` of the light's linear color at each node placing it (the node itself, named by the node when it has a name and else by the light or `light_N`; a node with a mesh too is a `Group` of the mesh and the light), `range` as `distance` (0 without), `decay` 2, a spot's `angle` its outer cone and `penumbra` 1 − inner / outer, and a directional or spot light aiming down the node's −Z at a `target` it holds at (0, 0, −1). Its `intensity` is the file's from API\_MINOR 23 (three.js r155+'s light units), and the file's over π at API\_MINOR 22, whose legacy units are π times those (spec rendering-and-quality.html#light-units): either way the model lights as three.js r185 lights it. A game declaring an older minor loads the model without its lights (named in the warning), whether the file uses or requires the extension (a required one failed to load before 1.20). Not applied: JPEG (before API\_MINOR 43) and other image formats (`KHR_texture_basisu`), `KHR_texture_transform` (before 1.44), UV sets past 0, other material extensions (clearcoat, transmission, sheen, … before 1.44), cameras, animations, skins and morph targets (since host API 1.40 morph targets load as three.js r185's GLTFLoader loads them: each primitive's POSITION and NORMAL targets, sparse or not, as relative `morphAttributes`, the mesh's `weights` and `extras.targetNames` as its influences and dictionary, a node's `weights` over them, and `weights` channels as `NAME.morphTargetInfluences` tracks). The rest of the model loads, and one console warning per model names all that was not applied (also in `ignored`), never silently. A file and its buffers are at most 64 MiB, and the document within the reader's limits (1,048,576 vertices and 3,145,728 indices per primitive, 4,096 primitives, 16,384 nodes, 256 images, 128 MiB of decoded buffers). From host API 1.44 (`PHYSICAL_MATERIAL_MINOR`) GLTFLoader is three.js r185's for physical materials: a material with KHR\_materials\_clearcoat, \_dispersion, \_iridescence, \_sheen, \_transmission, \_volume, \_ior, \_specular or \_anisotropy (and not unlit) is a `MeshPhysicalMaterial` with r185's settings for each (clearcoatFactor, clearcoatRoughnessFactor and their maps, clearcoatNormalMap with `clearcoatNormalScale` (scale, scale); dispersion (default 0); iridescence, iridescenceIOR, the thickness range (default \[100, 400\]) and maps; sheen 1 with sheenColor (default black), sheenRoughness (default 0) and maps; transmission and its map; thickness (default 0), thicknessMap, attenuationDistance (default Infinity) and attenuationColor; ior (default 1.5, 0 read as 1000); specularIntensity (default 1), specularColor and the specularIntensityMap and specularColorMap; anisotropy, anisotropyRotation and anisotropyMap), sheenColorMap and specularColorMap in `SRGBColorSpace` and the rest linear, as r185 sets them; such extensions may be required. A map's `KHR_texture_transform` gives it a texture of its own (r185's clone; each texture, transform and colour space loaded once more) with the transform's offset, rotation and scale as `offset`, `rotation` and `repeat`, and moves its `texCoord`. UVs are glTF's as written, every texture's `flipY` false; a primitive's `TANGENT` is its geometry's `tangent` (the physical program's vertex tangent, skinned as r185 skins it); and each primitive's material is r185's assignFinalMaterial's: without `TANGENT` a clone whose `normalScale.y` (and a physical one's `clearcoatNormalScale.y`) is negated, with `COLOR_0` one with `vertexColors`, one clone for each material and need; a material with a normal map on a primitive with `TANGENT` draws through the engine's physical program, which reads the vertex tangent (the built-in material derives its frame from the UVs). Below 1.44 these extensions, transforms and tangents are noted as not applied, and refused when required, as before. Remote files (the document and its external buffers) are fetched first (since API\_MINOR 7, see `files`). Rejects with a TypeError for a bad path, `NotFoundError` for a missing file, `SyntaxError` for a document it cannot read (or a required extension it lacks), and a RangeError with 128 loads already waiting.

```ts
export class GLTFLoader { … }
```

- `constructor();`

- `setPath(path: string): this;`

  A prefix for the paths given to `load` and `loadAsync`.

- `setKTX2Loader(loader: KTX2Loader | null): this;`

  three.js r185's: the KTX2Loader for `KHR_texture_basisu` images (since host API 1.43; undefined before). The engine reads KTX2 images itself, so the loader given changes nothing and none is needed: from host API 1.43 GLTFLoader loads KTX2 images of BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5 and BC7 blocks without supercompression (a texture's `KHR_texture_basisu` image first, then its WebP and core images where one fails, as Basis Universal ETC1S and UASTC images do), held as blocks where the device samples the format and unpacked to RGBA8 where not, counting what they hold (mips included) against the image budget; it loads the copy `starhermit package` made of a `.glb` or `.gltf` with `engine.textures.compress=bc` (`<file>.glb.ktx2.glb` or `<file>.gltf.ktx2.gltf`, e.g. `car.glb.ktx2.glb`, its embedded images compressed) in its place, and the KTX2 file packaged beside an external PNG or WebP image (`<image>.ktx2`) in the image's.

- `loadAsync(path: string): Promise<GLTF>;`
- `load(path: string, onLoad?: (gltf: GLTF) => void, onProgress?: unknown, onError?: (error: Error) => void): void;`

## Geometry

### AttributeArray

*type*

```ts
export type AttributeArray = Float32Array | Uint32Array | Uint16Array | Int16Array | Uint8Array | Int8Array;
```

Vertex data for meshes. Uploaded on first use; at most 1,048,576 vertices and 3,145,728 indices (RangeError); attributes are copied when set.

### BufferAttribute

*class*

```ts
export class BufferAttribute { … }
```

- `constructor(array: AttributeArray, itemSize: number, normalized?: boolean);`

  Integer arrays with `normalized` read as -1..1 (signed: `max(v / 127, -1)`, `max(v / 32767, -1)`) or 0..1 (unsigned: `v / 255`, `v / 65535`), as three.js: compact positions (Int16, scaled by the mesh), normals and colors (Int8, Uint8) stay compact in the game's heap (Int8, Uint8, Int16 and normalized since API\_MINOR 7).

  Before API\_MINOR 15 the runtime converts every attribute to floats as it uploads (32 bytes a vertex, 48 with colors, 64 with `custom`). From API\_MINOR 15 (`engine.minor=15`) the GPU keeps them as given, each in whole 4 bytes, and the mesh budget counts that:

  - Float32Array: floats (position and normal 12 bytes, uv 8, color and custom 16);
  - normalized Int8Array, Uint8Array, Int16Array, Uint16Array: 8- or 16-bit integers the GPU reads as above, exactly as three.js reads them: four components (4 or 8 bytes), uv two (4 bytes either way);
  - positions only, not normalized: Int16Array, Uint16Array, Int8Array, Uint8Array as the whole numbers they are (8 or 4 bytes), drawn within 0.01 of their value (scale them with the mesh, as before); hooks read them as given;
  - anything else (Uint32Array, or integers not normalized outside positions) as floats, as before.

  A three-value color's alpha is 1. Iron Curtain's models (Int16 positions, normalized Int8 normals and Uint8 colors) take 16 bytes a vertex where floats took 48, 20 with normalized Uint16 UVs; a geometry without `uv` stores none (it reads (0, 0), as before).

- `get array(): AttributeArray;`

  The values. Setting null releases them (three.js's pattern, in `onUpload`): the GPU keeps its copy, which draws on, `count` stays, and reading or writing the values, or uploading the geometry again, is a TypeError (change it with a new BufferAttribute). Setting an array of the same type and length replaces them. Since API\_MINOR 7.

- `set array(value: AttributeArray | null);`
- `readonly itemSize: number;`
- `readonly normalized: boolean;`
- `readonly count: number;`

- `onUpload(callback: (this: BufferAttribute) => void): this;`

  Called, with the attribute as `this`, once its values reached the GPU (three.js `onUpload`; since API\_MINOR 7): `attribute.onUpload(function () { this.array = null; })` lets them go from the game's heap. Compute bounding volumes first (`computeBoundingSphere`); picking keeps working from the runtime's own copy.

- `needsUpdate: boolean;`

  Set after changing `array` to re-upload the geometry (or, for an instanced mesh's `instanceMatrix` and `instanceColor`, the instances, in one host call).

- `addUpdateRange(offset: number, count: number): void;`

  Limits the next upload to `count` items from `offset` (three.js's `updateRange`/`addUpdateRange`).

- `clearUpdateRanges(): void;`

- `getX(index: number): number;`

  Item `index`'s components (normalized values as numbers, written back as the array's integers), as three.js.

- `getY(index: number): number;`
- `getZ(index: number): number;`
- `getW(index: number): number;`
- `setX(index: number, x: number): this;`
- `setY(index: number, y: number): this;`
- `setZ(index: number, z: number): this;`
- `setXY(index: number, x: number, y: number): this;`
- `setXYZ(index: number, x: number, y: number, z: number): this;`
- `setXYZW(index: number, x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number): this;`

- `clone(): BufferAttribute;`

  A copy with its own values.

Since API\_MINOR 18.

- `setW(index: number, w: number): this;`
- `getComponent(index: number, component: number): number;`
- `setComponent(index: number, component: number, value: number): this;`

- `copyAt(index1: number, attribute: BufferAttribute, index2: number): this;`

  Item `index2` of `attribute` into item `index1` (raw values).

- `copyArray(array: ArrayLike<number>): this;`

  Raw values from an array (it must fit).

- `set(value: ArrayLike<number>, offset?: number): this;`

  Raw values from an array at `offset` (it must fit).

- `copy(source: BufferAttribute): this;`

  A copy of `source`'s values, item size, normalization, name and usage (its count becomes `source`'s).

- `applyMatrix3(m: Matrix3): this;`

  Each item (two or three components) times the matrix.

- `applyMatrix4(m: Matrix4): this;`

  Each item a point times the matrix.

- `applyNormalMatrix(m: Matrix3): this;`

  Each item a normal times a normal matrix, normalized.

- `transformDirection(m: Matrix4): this;`

  Each item a direction turned by the matrix, normalized.

- `name: string;`

- `usage: number;`

  three.js's usage hint (`StaticDrawUsage`, `DynamicDrawUsage`): kept, the engine uploads what changed either way.

- `setUsage(usage: number): this;`
- `toJSON(): { itemSize: number; type: string; array: number[]; normalized: boolean };`
- `dispose(): void;`

### InterleavedBuffer

*class*

Items of `stride` floats sharing one Float32Array (three.js r185's InterleavedBuffer; since API\_MINOR 33, a TypeError before): each of its InterleavedBufferAttributes reads `itemSize` floats at its `offset` within every item. A geometry whose attributes all share one buffer crosses into the runtime as that one array, read there where its attributes lie: the GPU holds the same mesh, byte for byte and in the same mesh bytes, as separate Float32 BufferAttributes of those values would make (positions 12 bytes a vertex, normals 12, uv 8, color and custom 16), so the game never splits its vertices into arrays of their own. Float32Array only; at most 4,096 floats an item.

```ts
export class InterleavedBuffer { … }
```

- `constructor(array: Float32Array, stride: number);`
- `readonly isInterleavedBuffer: true;`

- `get array(): Float32Array;`

  The values. Setting null releases them (in `onUpload`, as a BufferAttribute's): the GPU keeps its copy, which draws on, and reading them, or uploading the geometry again, is a TypeError. Setting a Float32Array of the same length replaces them.

- `set array(value: Float32Array | null);`
- `stride: number;`

- `readonly count: number;`

  Its items: the array's length over the stride.

- `version: number;`
- `readonly uuid: string;`
- `usage: number;`

- `needsUpdate: boolean;`

  Set after changing the values to upload the geometry again.

- `setUsage(usage: number): this;`

- `readonly updateRanges: { start: number; count: number }[];`

  three.js's partial-update hint, kept and cleared as three.js does: a changed buffer uploads whole. For bounded uploads of a large geometry use a StreamingGeometry's pages.

- `addUpdateRange(start: number, count: number): void;`
- `clearUpdateRanges(): void;`

- `onUpload(callback: (this: InterleavedBuffer) => void): this;`

  Called, with the buffer as `this`, once per upload of a geometry using it (three.js calls the buffer's, not its attributes'): `buffer.onUpload(function () { this.array = null; })` lets the values go from the game's heap.

- `copy(source: InterleavedBuffer): this;`
- `copyAt(index1: number, interleavedBuffer: InterleavedBuffer, index2: number): this;`
- `set(value: ArrayLike<number>, offset?: number): this;`

- `clone(data?: object): InterleavedBuffer;`

  A buffer over a copy of the values; buffers of one ArrayBuffer cloned with the same `data` share one copy (three.js).

- `toJSON(data?: object): { uuid: string; buffer: string; type: string; stride: number };`

Its values are its buffer's: `array`, `count`, `needsUpdate` and `onUpload` are the buffer's.

### BufferGeometry

*class*

```ts
export class BufferGeometry { … }
```

- `constructor();`

- `readonly type: string;`

  three.js's: `"BufferGeometry"`, or the built geometry's class name (since API\_MINOR 20; before, only the shapes of API\_MINOR 17 and later had one).

- `setAttribute(name: AttributeName, attribute: GeometryAttribute): this;`

  `position` (3), `normal` (3), `uv` (2), `color` (3 or 4, linear; any finite values: shading clamps color to 0–65504 and alpha to 0–1, custom materials read them as they are) and `custom` (1 to 4 numbers a vertex, zeros after them; read only by custom materials as `Vertex.custom`, since API\_MINOR 6); `tangent` (4, what `computeTangents` makes; since API\_MINOR 20) is kept and not drawn; `skinIndex` and `skinWeight` (4 a vertex: a SkinnedMesh's joints and weights; since API\_MINOR 25); other names throw a TypeError. Since API\_MINOR 33 an InterleavedBufferAttribute too.

- `getAttribute(name: AttributeName): GeometryAttribute | undefined;`

- `morphAttributes: { position?: BufferAttribute[]; normal?: BufferAttribute[]; [name: string]: BufferAttribute[] | undefined };`

  Morph targets (since host API 1.40, three.js r185's): `position` (and `normal`) lists of attributes, one a target, each as many vertices as the geometry; a target's `name` keys its mesh's `morphTargetDictionary`. Meshes morph by their `morphTargetInfluences` in every pass's vertex stage (shadows and depth too), before skinning, through a morph texture (up to 1,024 targets and 2,048 rows of 2,048 texels: a header, the joints, and three texels a vertex a target, six with normals); one that does not fit is morphed on the CPU (a console warning once). Bounds (`computeBoundingBox`, `computeBoundingSphere`) take the targets in at full influence, as three.js's do. Copied and cloned with the geometry. `color` targets are not drawn.

- `morphTargetsRelative: boolean;`

  Whether the targets are displacements (true, as glTF's) or positions (false, three.js's default; the base then weighs 1 − the influences' sum). Since host API 1.40.

- `setFromPoints(points: readonly (Vector2 | Vector3)[]): this;`

  A float `position` attribute of the points (z 0 for Vector2s), or, when there is one, its first vertices set to them (as many as it holds; a warning past it), as three.js (since API\_MINOR 20): `new BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(curve.getPoints(50))` for a `Line`.

- `lookAt(vector: Vector3): this;`

  Turns the positions (and normals) to face `vector` from the origin, as an Object3D's `lookAt` (since API\_MINOR 20).

- `normalizeNormals(): void;`

  Each normal made unit length (since API\_MINOR 20).

- `computeTangents(): void;`

  A `tangent` attribute (x, y, z and the handedness w) from the index, positions, normals and UVs over the groups, as three.js computes it (since API\_MINOR 20); without them it logs an error and does nothing.

- `setIndex(index: BufferAttribute | readonly number[] | null): this;`

  Without an index the vertices draw in order, three a triangle; from API\_MINOR 15 the GPU holds no index list for them (before, the runtime made one, 4 bytes a vertex).

- `getIndex(): BufferAttribute | null;`

- `readonly index: BufferAttribute | null;`

  The index (`getIndex()`) and the attributes by name, as three.js has them.

- `readonly attributes: Readonly<Record<string, GeometryAttribute>>;`
- `computeVertexNormals(): void;`

- `computeBoundingSphere(): void;`

  Model-space bounding sphere (for culling, picking and shadows): a Sphere since API\_MINOR 18.

- `boundingBox: Box3 | null;`

  The box around the positions (since API\_MINOR 18; null until `computeBoundingBox`, which `Box3.setFromObject` calls).

- `computeBoundingBox(): void;`

- `boundingSphere: Sphere | { center: Vector3; radius: number } | null;`

  Culls the geometry's meshes when set (since API\_MINOR 7), in place of a sphere around its vertices: set or inflate it when a custom material's vertex hook moves vertices past them (skinning, wind). Null (the default) culls by the vertices. One with NaN or infinite values, or an empty one (a negative radius), culls nothing, as three.js draws such meshes (earlier engines threw). Changing it changes how the meshes cull, without uploading the geometry again (since 1.33's fix, every minor; before, it uploaded it again from its values, a TypeError once `onUpload` had released them). A geometry without attributes (see `drawRange`) culls by it alone: without it, it is never culled.

- `translate(x: number, y: number, z: number): this;`
- `rotateX(angle: number): this;`
- `rotateY(angle: number): this;`
- `rotateZ(angle: number): this;`
- `scale(x: number, y: number, z: number): this;`

- `applyMatrix4(matrix: Matrix4): this;`

  Transforms positions (and normals by its normal matrix, normalized), then recomputes the bounds it has (three.js).

- `applyQuaternion(quaternion: Quaternion): this;`

- `center(): this;`

  Moves the positions so the bounding box's center is the origin (three.js; it computes `boundingBox`).

- `toNonIndexed(): BufferGeometry;`

  Each triangle its own three vertices (no index).

- `clone(): BufferGeometry;`

  A BufferGeometry with copies of the attributes, index, groups, bounds and (since API\_MINOR 18) draw range and name.

- `copy(source: BufferGeometry): this;`

  Copies of `source`'s attributes, index, groups, bounds and draw range, its name, and its userData shared (three.js).

- `name: string;`
- `userData: Record<string, unknown>;`

- `dispose(): void;`

  Releases the GPU mesh (it is made again if drawn).

- `readonly drawRange: { start: number; count: number };`

  Which elements draw, as three.js draws them: `count` from `start` (`count` Infinity, the default, to the end), of the index when the geometry has one, else of its vertices in order (three a triangle). `Points` draw the range's vertices, `Line`, `LineSegments` and `LineLoop` its vertices or indices, and since API\_MINOR 18 a `Mesh` (an `InstancedMesh`'s every instance, and a material array's groups within it) draws the range too, natively and in browsers (before, meshes with attributes drew all). Changing it only changes the draw: nothing is uploaded again, so a ribbon or a trail can fill a buffer ahead and extend its range each frame. A range past the geometry draws what lies within it; rays hit only the range's triangles.

  A geometry with no `position` (and no other attribute or index) draws `count` vertices, three a triangle, for a custom material's vertex hook to place from `vertex_index()` (0 to `count - 1`) and the instance's data (since API\_MINOR 15, as three.js draws such a geometry; before, it drew nothing): `geometry.setDrawRange(0, 405504)`. It costs no mesh bytes (it counts as a mesh), its vertices read position (0, 0, 0), normal (0, 1, 0) and uv (0, 0) until the hook sets them (the built-in materials draw nothing), raycasts pass through it, and it culls by `boundingSphere` alone. `start` must be 0 and `count` a whole multiple of 3 of at most 1,048,576 (TypeError, RangeError).

- `setDrawRange(start: number, count: number): void;`

- `groups: { start: number; count: number; materialIndex: number }[];`

  Ranges of the index (of the vertices without one), each drawn with the `materialIndex`th material of a mesh's material array (three.js; since API\_MINOR 17). A mesh with one material draws the whole geometry whatever its groups. Copied by `clone`, `copy` and `toNonIndexed`. Each group draws a range of the geometry's one uploaded mesh (since 1.33's fix, at every minor from 18: before, each group was a mesh of its own made from the CPU values, so groups or a material array set after `onUpload` released them threw a TypeError, and each group held another copy of the vertices on the GPU); an indexed geometry without normals in a game before API\_MINOR 33 keeps a mesh a group, its normals made from the group's triangles as before.

- `addGroup(start: number, count: number, materialIndex?: number): void;`
- `clearGroups(): void;`

### StreamingGeometry

*class*

A geometry the engine holds in pages (StarHermit's; since API\_MINOR 33, a TypeError before; three.js has none): each page's interleaved vertices, and with an index capacity its own indices numbering them (0 its first vertex), go to the GPU when `addPage` takes them, a mesh of their own read once from the page (no copy kept in the game's heap, none made there), and the geometry draws its pages in order as one, up to the capacity it declares. A page is one upload of at most 1,048,576 vertices and 3,145,728 indices (and the frame's 96 MiB upload bound; pages made past it wait for the next frames, drawn once sent), so a model of any size within the mesh budget streams in over as many frames as its pages, and `setPage` replaces one page alone (a bounded update). With `transfer` the engine takes the page's ArrayBuffers (the vertices', and the indices' if they have one of their own): detached once read, their memory let go at once, as a worker message's transfer list does; they must be ArrayBuffers of their own (TypeError before anything is read).

Its attributes are InterleavedBufferAttributes of `buffer` (stride floats a vertex, holding no values), set before the first page; `position` (3 floats) is required. `drawRange` and `groups` count the pages' elements (indices, or vertices without them) one page after another; a material array draws them, as a BufferGeometry's. Each page counts as a mesh against the mesh budget and its bytes as any geometry's (the same as separate Float32 attributes); at most 256 pages (RangeError), and a mesh draws at most 256 parts (a group spanning pages takes one a page). Rays hit its pages; frustum culling takes each page's own bounds. Its values are the engine's: `copy`, `clone`, `applyMatrix4` (and `translate` & co.), `computeVertexNormals` and `toNonIndexed` throw a TypeError; it draws on a Mesh (not as points, lines, an instanced or a skinned mesh, nor as a wireframe: TypeError).

```ts
export class StreamingGeometry extends BufferGeometry { … }
```

- `constructor(stride: number, capacity: { vertices: number; indices?: number });`

  `stride` floats a vertex; `capacity.vertices` 1 to 268,435,456 and `capacity.indices` 0 (pages without indices, the default) to 805,306,368 (RangeError).

- `readonly isStreamingGeometry: true;`
- `readonly buffer: InterleavedBuffer;`
- `readonly capacity: Readonly<{ vertices: number; indices: number }>;`
- `readonly vertexCount: number;`
- `readonly indexCount: number;`
- `readonly pageCount: number;`

- `addPage(vertices: Float32Array, indices?: Uint16Array | Uint32Array | null, transfer?: boolean): number;`

  Adds and uploads a page (whole vertices of the stride; indices, Uint16Array or Uint32Array, exactly when the capacity has some): a RangeError past the capacity or the page bounds, a TypeError for a bad page, nothing taken either way. Returns its number.

- `setPage(page: number, vertices: Float32Array, indices?: Uint16Array | Uint32Array | null, transfer?: boolean): this;`

  Replaces page `page` (its old mesh let go), as `addPage` takes one.

- `computeBoundingBox(): void;`

  The box around the pages' positions as the engine read them (exact).

- `computeBoundingSphere(): void;`

  The sphere about that box (its center, half its diagonal), which holds every position; null without pages.

- `dispose(): void;`

  Lets its pages go: it holds none afterwards.

### mergeGeometries

*function*

```ts
export function mergeGeometries(geometries: readonly BufferGeometry[], useGroups?: boolean): BufferGeometry | null;
```

One geometry from several (three.js's `BufferGeometryUtils. mergeGeometries`): they must share their attributes (all indexed or none); null when they do not. Bounded as any geometry (RangeError). `useGroups` (since API\_MINOR 17) adds a group for each geometry, its place in the list its material index.

three.js's built-in shapes with its parameters, defaults and vertex layout; their `position`, `normal` and `uv` attributes and index are readable (and writable) like any geometry's. Segment counts are at most 1,024 (RangeError). Since API\_MINOR 17 boxes, cylinders and cones have three.js's groups (a box's faces +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z as materials 0 to 5; a cylinder's side 0, top 1 and bottom 2), so material arrays work.

## Curves, paths and shapes (since API\_MINOR 17)

three.js r185's curves, paths, shapes and ShapeUtils, statement by statement: the points they give are three.js's, natively and in browsers. Since API\_MINOR 20 the 3D curves too (`LineCurve3`, `QuadraticBezierCurve3`, `CubicBezierCurve3`, `CatmullRomCurve3`), each curve's `computeFrenetFrames`, `toJSON` and `fromJSON`, and paths of 3D curves.

### CurveJSON

*interface*

What a curve's `toJSON` gives (three.js's): its `type`, `arcLengthDivisions` and each kind's own fields (vectors as arrays).

```ts
export interface CurveJSON { … }
```

- `metadata?: { version: number; type: string; generator: string };`
- `type: string;`
- `arcLengthDivisions: number;`
- `[key: string]: any;`

### FrenetFrames

*interface*

Frenet frames along a curve: a tangent, normal and binormal at each of `segments + 1` points spaced by arc length.

```ts
export interface FrenetFrames { … }
```

- `tangents: Vector3[];`
- `normals: Vector3[];`
- `binormals: Vector3[];`

### Curve

*class*

A curve, 2D (`T` Vector2, the default) or 3D (Vector3, since API\_MINOR 20): `getPoint(t)` for t from 0 to 1 (each kind its own), and from it points spaced by arc length (`arcLengthDivisions` samples), lengths and tangents. A subclass of your own overrides `getPoint`.

```ts
export class Curve<T extends Vector2 | Vector3 = Vector2> { … }
```

- `type: string;`
- `arcLengthDivisions: number;`
- `needsUpdate: boolean;`
- `getPoint(t: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`
- `getPointAt(u: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`
- `getPoints(divisions?: number): T[];`
- `getSpacedPoints(divisions?: number): T[];`
- `getLength(): number;`
- `getLengths(divisions?: number): number[];`
- `updateArcLengths(): void;`
- `getUtoTmapping(u: number, distance?: number | null): number;`

- `getTangent(t: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`

  The unit tangent at `t`, from points 0.0001 either side (a Vector2 or Vector3 as the curve's points are; a line's exactly).

- `getTangentAt(u: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`

- `computeFrenetFrames(segments: number, closed?: boolean): FrenetFrames;`

  Tangents, normals and binormals at `segments + 1` points spaced by arc length (since API\_MINOR 20), as three.js computes them: the first normal across the first tangent's smallest axis, carried along by the turn between tangents; `closed` twists them evenly so the last meets the first. What TubeGeometry and ExtrudeGeometry's `extrudePath` follow.

- `clone(): this;`
- `copy(source: Curve<any>): this;`

- `toJSON(): CurveJSON;`

  Since API\_MINOR 20.

- `fromJSON(json: CurveJSON): this;`

  Since API\_MINOR 20: the curve set from `toJSON`'s data.

### CurvePath

*class*

Curves end to end, 2D or (since API\_MINOR 20) 3D. `getPoints(divisions)` (default 12) divides each curve by `divisions` (an ellipse or arc by twice it, a line not at all, a spline by it times its points), leaving out a point equal to the one before; past 1,048,576 points it is a RangeError. `fromJSON` makes each curve of its type (one of the curve classes above; another is a TypeError).

```ts

```

- `add(curve: Curve<T>): void;`

- `closePath(): this;`

  Joins the end back to the start with a line (a LineCurve, or a LineCurve3 for 3D points), if they differ.

- `getCurveLengths(): number[];`

### ExtrudeGeometryOptions

*interface*

`ExtrudeGeometry`'s settings, three.js's defaults: `depth` 1, `bevelEnabled` true, `bevelThickness` 0.2, `bevelSize` `bevelThickness - 0.1`, `bevelOffset` 0, `bevelSegments` 3, `curveSegments` 12, `steps` 1 (`steps` at least 1 and `bevelSegments` whole numbers up to 1,024: fractions are dropped). Since API\_MINOR 20, `extrudePath` extrudes along a 3D curve instead of +Z (`steps` layers at its `getSpacedPoints(steps)`, each shape point (x, y) placed along the frame's normal and binormal of `computeFrenetFrames(steps, closed)`, closed for a closed CatmullRomCurve3; no bevel and `depth` unused, as three.js), and a custom `UVGenerator` gives the UVs (before, either was a TypeError).

```ts
export interface ExtrudeGeometryOptions { … }
```

- `curveSegments?: number;`
- `steps?: number;`
- `depth?: number;`
- `bevelEnabled?: boolean;`
- `bevelThickness?: number;`
- `bevelSize?: number;`
- `bevelOffset?: number;`
- `bevelSegments?: number;`
- `extrudePath?: Curve<Vector3>;`
- `UVGenerator?: UVGenerator;`

### UVGenerator

*interface*

An ExtrudeGeometry's UVs of your own (three.js's `UVGenerator`; since API\_MINOR 20): called for each cap triangle and side quad in three.js's order with the positions (x, y, z a vertex, as three.js holds them before rounding to 32-bit floats: the whole geometry's, where three.js passes those made so far) and the vertices' numbers; three UVs a triangle and four a quad (a, b, c, d).

```ts
export interface UVGenerator { … }
```

- `generateTopUV(geometry: ExtrudeGeometry, vertices: number[], indexA: number, indexB: number, indexC: number): Vector2[];`
- `generateSideWallUV(geometry: ExtrudeGeometry, vertices: number[], indexA: number, indexB: number, indexC: number, indexD: number): Vector2[];`

### ExtrudeGeometry

*class*

Shapes extruded from z = 0 to `depth` along +Z, their edges bevelled outward (three.js `ExtrudeGeometry`): triangles not indexed, flat normals, UVs as three.js's `WorldUVGenerator`, and for each shape a group of its front and back caps (material 0) and one of its sides (material 1), so `new Mesh(geometry, [face, side])` works. Default: a unit square. Past 1,048,576 vertices it is a RangeError.

```ts

```

- `constructor(shapes?: Shape | Shape[], options?: ExtrudeGeometryOptions);`
- `readonly type: "ExtrudeGeometry";`
- `readonly parameters: { shapes: Shape | Shape[]; options: ExtrudeGeometryOptions };`

*class*

A geometry's edges where its faces meet at more than `thresholdAngle` degrees (default 1), and its open edges, as three.js computes them (points within 1e-4 one point; edges in three.js's order): `position` holds two vertices an edge, for `LineSegments`. A box gives its 12 edges.

```ts

```

### WireframeGeometry

*class*

Every triangle's edges, each once whichever way round (three.js `WireframeGeometry`, since API\_MINOR 18): `position` holds two vertices an edge, for `LineSegments`. An indexed geometry's groups are read in turn (its whole index without groups).

## Polyhedra, lathe, torus knot and rounded box (since API\_MINOR 18)

three.js r185's, built as it builds them: positions, normals, UVs, index and groups are three.js's, bit for bit. Segment counts are whole numbers (fractions dropped) of 1 to 1,024, and a geometry past 1,048,576 vertices is refused before it is made (RangeError).

### TubeGeometry

*class*

A tube of `radius` (default 1) round a 3D curve (three.js `TubeGeometry`; since API\_MINOR 20): `tubularSegments` (default 64) rings spaced along `path` by arc length, each of `radialSegments` (default 8) round the curve's Frenet frame there (`path.computeFrenetFrames(tubularSegments, closed)`, kept as `tangents`, `normals` and `binormals`); a `closed` tube's last ring is its first again. Indexed; UVs along (u) then round (v). Default: a quadratic Bézier from (-1, -1, 0) through (-1, 1, 0) to (1, 1, 0). Segment counts are whole numbers of 1 to 1,024 (else RangeError); built from a new curve or new segments, as three.js (a trail that grows makes a new one, or draws a range of one made long enough).

Not indexed, a group a face as a box's (+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z); at `segments` 0 three.js's unit box, whatever the size.

### Sky

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 40 (`SKY_MINOR`; absent before): three.js r185's addon `Sky` (examples/jsm/objects/Sky.js), exported here as the engine has no addons path (and from `starhermit:sky` too): Preetham's analytic daylight over a unit box seen from inside, with r185's clouds and sun disc, its program in WGSL. Its box's corners go to the far plane (three.js's `gl_Position.z = gl_Position.w`, a hair inside it), so `sky.scale.setScalar(450000)` shows it whatever the camera's far; it is not frustum-culled. Set it through `sky.material.uniforms` as in three.js: `turbidity` (2), `rayleigh` (1), `mieCoefficient` (0.005), `mieDirectionalG` (0.8), `sunPosition` (a Vector3), `up` ((0, 1, 0)), `cloudScale` (0.0002), `cloudSpeed` (0.0001), `cloudCoverage` (0.4), `cloudDensity` (0.4), `cloudElevation` (0.5), `showSunDisc` (1) and `time` (0). Its light is linear and tone mapped as three.js's (`tonemapping_fragment`). For a physically based sky with the time of day see `starhermit:sky`'s `SkyAtmosphere`.

## Materials

### MaterialParameters

*interface*

```ts
export interface MaterialParameters { … }
```

- `color?: ColorInput;`

  Base color (default white), linear; components above 1 (three.js HDR colors, up to 65504) light brighter than white, which tone mapping and bloom take.

- `map?: Texture | null;`

  Base color texture, multiplied by `color`.

- `opacity?: number;`

  0–1 (default 1). Below 1 needs `transparent` to blend.

- `transparent?: boolean;`

  Draws after opaque objects, sorted farthest first, blending as `blending` says (normal by default). Before API\_MINOR 20 blending other than normal draws there whatever this says; from it, as in three.js, this alone decides.

- `alphaTest?: number;`

  Above 0, pixels whose alpha is below it are discarded (masked).

- `blending?: Blending;`

- `blendEquation?: number;`

  With `CustomBlending` (since API\_MINOR 10): the color's equation (default `AddEquation`) and factors (default `SrcAlphaFactor` and `OneMinusSrcAlphaFactor`), and the alpha's (null, the default: the color's).

- `blendSrc?: number;`
- `blendDst?: number;`
- `blendEquationAlpha?: number | null;`
- `blendSrcAlpha?: number | null;`
- `blendDstAlpha?: number | null;`
- `side?: Side;`

- `shadowSide?: Side | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 23: see `Material.shadowSide`.

- `depthWrite?: boolean;`

  Default from API\_MINOR 20: true, as three.js's for every material, transparent ones included. Before it: written unless blended, so a port declaring an older minor that relied on a transparent mesh's depth writes sets `depthWrite: true` (grid lines drawn before a glass top under them stay visible only where they wrote depth, as blended meshes draw farthest first).

- `depthTest?: boolean;`

  Whether the depth test applies (default true); without it the material draws whatever is nearer and writes no depth, as in three.js, whatever its `depthFunc`.

- `colorWrite?: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 35: see `Material.colorWrite`.

- `forceSinglePass?: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 42: see `Material.forceSinglePass`.

- `depthFunc?: DepthModes;`

  The depth test's comparison (three.js `depthFunc`; a `DepthModes` constant such as `LessDepth`). Default: `LessEqualDepth` from API\_MINOR 20 (three.js's, so of two coplanar surfaces the later drawn shows), `LessDepth` before it (the earlier drawn shows). A value set is honoured at every minor: `LessDepth` keeps minor 19's coplanar result for a model whose faces were baked over each other. Shadow maps keep the nearer test. Another value is a TypeError at the frame's sync. Since engine 1.20.2 (any minor).

- `fog?: boolean;`

  Whether the scene's fog applies (default true).

- `vertexColors?: boolean;`

  Multiply by the geometry's `color` attribute.

- `polygonOffset?: boolean;`
- `polygonOffsetFactor?: number;`
- `polygonOffsetUnits?: number;`
- `visible?: boolean;`

- `premultipliedAlpha?: boolean;`

  With `transparent` and normal blending: the output's color times its alpha over earlier output times one minus the alpha (three.js `premultipliedAlpha`; since API\_MINOR 7). A built-in material's color is premultiplied for it; a ShaderMaterial's fragment gives its color premultiplied, so alpha 0 adds light (glows and smoke in one material).

- `toneMapped?: boolean;`

  Whether the output is tone mapped (default true; post effects tone map everything). Since API\_MINOR 6.

- `hooks?: MaterialHooks | null;`

  Hooks into the material's shading (since API\_MINOR 6).

### Material

*class*

Common to all materials; changes apply from the next frame.

```ts
export abstract class Material { … }
```

- `#private;`

- `readonly id: number;`

  three.js's (since API\_MINOR 20): a number of its own, in the order materials are made; from API\_MINOR 20 it orders the opaque list after render order.

- `name: string;`
- `userData: Record<string, unknown>;`
- `color: Color;`
- `map: Texture | null;`
- `opacity: number;`
- `transparent: boolean;`
- `alphaTest: number;`
- `blending: Blending;`

- `blendEquation: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 10: see `MaterialParameters.blendEquation`.

- `blendSrc: number;`
- `blendDst: number;`
- `blendEquationAlpha: number | null;`
- `blendSrcAlpha: number | null;`
- `blendDstAlpha: number | null;`
- `side: Side;`

- `shadowSide: Side | null;`

  The faces the shadow maps draw (three.js; since API\_MINOR 23): null (the default) draws the side opposite `side` (back faces of a front-sided material, front faces of a back-sided one, both of a double-sided one), so a surface facing the light is not in its own map and does not shadow itself. Before API\_MINOR 23 the maps draw the faces `side` draws, and this is ignored.

- `depthWrite: boolean;`
- `depthTest: boolean;`

- `colorWrite: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 35 (`COLOR_WRITE_MINOR`; absent before): three.js r185's `colorWrite` (default true). False draws no color: the material's draws still test and write depth as `depthTest` and `depthWrite` say (a depth-only occluder or mask, a depth prime); shadow maps and `renderer.sceneDepth` take it as before. Every backend masks the color target's writes in the draw's pipeline.

- `forceSinglePass: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 42 (`DOUBLE_SIDE_PASSES_MINOR`; absent before): three.js r185's `forceSinglePass` (default false). A transparent `DoubleSide` material draws each object twice, its back faces and then its front faces, so its far side shows through its near side as three.js draws it; true draws it once with both sides, as older games' do. Shadow maps draw it once either way.

- `receiveDecals: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 43 (`DECALS_MINOR`; absent before), ENGINE EXTENSION: whether `DecalProjector`s land on this material's surfaces (default true). False (units over a scorched ground) marks its opaque surfaces in the scene-depth prepass (blue 1 in `renderer.sceneDepth`, 0 elsewhere), which decals read to leave them alone.

- `distortion: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 43 (`DISTORTION_MINOR`; absent before), ENGINE EXTENSION: the material distorts what lies behind it (default false). For a transparent material sampling `renderer.sceneColor`: when every object of a frame sampling it has `distortion`, the colour is copied before the first of them instead of before the first transparent object, so it holds the transparent objects drawn before them too (heat shimmer bending fire and smoke). Objects that sample it without `distortion` keep the older copy for all. See `DistortionMaterial`.

- `depthFunc: DepthModes;`

  Since engine 1.20.2 (any minor): see `MaterialParameters.depthFunc`. Reads the default the game's minor takes until one is set.

- `fog: boolean;`
- `vertexColors: boolean;`
- `polygonOffset: boolean;`
- `polygonOffsetFactor: number;`
- `polygonOffsetUnits: number;`
- `visible: boolean;`

- `envMap: Texture | null;`

  An environment this material reflects instead of `scene.environment` (standard, physical, Lambert and, since API\_MINOR 29, Phong materials; see `PMREMGenerator`).

- `toneMapped: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: whether the output is tone mapped (three.js `toneMapped`, default true; without post effects only).

- `premultipliedAlpha: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 7: see `MaterialParameters.premultipliedAlpha`.

- `hooks: MaterialHooks | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: the game's WGSL hooked into this material's shading (standard, physical, Lambert and basic materials, and Phong, toon and matcap ones since API\_MINOR 29; see `MaterialHooks`), or null. Assign a new object, or change its sources or uniforms' types, and the material's program follows from the next frame; uniform values are read every frame.

- `readonly shaderError: string | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: why the material's program was refused, as `part:line:column: message` (the part being `vertex`, `surface`, `vertexShader`, `fragmentShader`, `uniforms` or `engine`), or null. A refused program leaves the material drawing without it (a `ShaderMaterial` draws nothing) and is logged once. The engine checks the code by the rules browsers' WebGPU enforces, but a browser's WebGPU compiles the program again as the game draws on and may still refuse it some frames later: the game's log then says so once (with WebGPU's message at the part, line and column), and `shaderError` reports it from then on.

- `compile(): void;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: compiles the material's program now (otherwise it compiles when first drawn), throwing a SyntaxError with `shaderError`'s message if it is refused.

- `clone(): this;`

  A material of the same class with this one's settings: colors and vectors copied, textures shared (three.js); since API\_MINOR 18 its userData copied by JSON and a ShaderMaterial's uniforms cloned.

- `copy(source: Material): this;`

  `source`'s settings, as `clone` takes them (since API\_MINOR 18).

- `dispose(): void;`

## Custom materials (since API\_MINOR 6)

A game's WGSL (the WebGPU shading language; the subset starhermit-shader compiles: no while, pointers or atomics; `switch` since engine 1.43, at every API\_MINOR) joined with the engine's mesh stages and compiled for every backend (SPIR-V, HLSL, GLSL ES 3.00, WGSL), so the same code draws on Vulkan, Direct3D 12, Metal, OpenGL ES and WebGPU. A material's parts (its hooks, or a ShaderMaterial's vertexShader, fragmentShader and fogShader) are one module, each stage compiled from all of them: a struct, const or helper function declared in one part is visible in the others and is declared once (a second declaration of the name is an error, "declared twice in one scope"). It is sandboxed: a part declares structs, constants and functions only (no variables, bindings, entry points or attributes, no names the engine declares, nothing starting with `_`), reads no engine globals but `uniforms` and its textures, and loops only with `for (var i = A; i < B; i++)` over constant bounds and step (any of &lt;, &lt;=, &gt;, &gt;=, ++, --, += k, -= k; at most 65,536 iterations, nested loops together); WGSL has no recursion. Derivatives (dpdx, dpdy, fwidth), textureSample and textureSampleBias stay in uniform control flow (outside branches and loops on per-pixel values; branching on `uniforms` and constants is fine), as WebGPU requires; vertex code samples with textureSampleLevel or textureSampleGrad and cannot discard. textureSampleBias, textureSampleGrad (explicit gradients, so anywhere) and textureDimensions (a texture's size, or a mip level's) work on every backend since API\_MINOR 8. Each part is at most 64 KiB. Errors name the part and its own line and column.

What the engine declares for a game's code:

```text
struct Vertex { position: vec3f, normal: vec3f, uv: vec2f,
  color: vec4f, custom: vec4f, instance: vec4f, clip: vec4f,
  v0: vec4f, v1: vec4f, v2: vec4f, v3: vec4f,
  instance_color: vec4f, vertex_color: vec4f,
  instance1: vec4f, instance2: vec4f, instance3: vec4f,
  skin_index: vec4u, skin_weight: vec4f, bind_position: vec3f }
  position and normal in object space (skinned already on a
  skinned mesh); color the instance color times
  the vertex color (when the material has vertexColors; white
  otherwise), each also given alone (instance_color, which includes
  the InstancedMesh's color, 0..65504, and vertex_color: a game may
  carry data in them and set color itself); custom the
  geometry's `custom` attribute (zeros without one); instance the
  InstancedMesh's `instanceCustom` slot 0 and instance1..3 its slots
  1 to 3 (zeros otherwise; an animated InstancedSkinnedMesh's
  slot 3 is its animation state, see InstancedSkinnedMesh);
  skin_index and skin_weight the geometry's `skinIndex` (whole
  numbers 0..65535) and `skinWeight` (0..1, in 1/65535 steps) on a
  SkinnedMesh or an InstancedSkinnedMesh (since API_MINOR 43,
  SKIN_ATTRIBUTES_MINOR; zeros on other meshes); bind_position
  (since API_MINOR 45, HOOK_BIND_POSITION_MINOR; before it the
  member is the game's error) the geometry's position before
  skinning and morph targets on a SkinnedMesh or an
  InstancedSkinnedMesh (`position` itself elsewhere): a hook may
  mix the rest pose in, or key effects to it; clip zero, or
  set by the hook (w not 0) to place the vertex in clip space itself
  (depth -1..1 as view_projection() gives; the shadow pass ignores
  it); v0..v3 four varyings for the fragment stage.
struct Surface { base_color: vec4f, emissive: vec3f, metalness: f32,
  roughness: f32, normal: vec3f, occlusion: f32, world: vec3f,
  uv: vec2f, color: vec4f, v0..v3: vec4f, front: bool }
  (A MeshPhysicalMaterial's since API_MINOR 44 also has iridescence,
  iridescence_thickness (nm), transmission and thickness: f32, its
  settings times its maps, which the hook may change.)
  base_color linear after the map, color, opacity and vertex colors;
  emissive linear after its intensity and map; normal in world space
  after the normal map; occlusion 0..1 (1 none). The rest describe the
  fragment (read-only), but v0..v3, which arrive as the vertex
  hook's varyings and go on, as the hook leaves them, to the light
  hook's Light.
struct Fragment { world: vec3f, normal: vec3f, uv: vec2f, color: vec4f,
  v0..v3: vec4f, front: bool, coord: vec4f }
  coord the fragment's window position (WGSL @builtin(position);
  rows from the top on every backend since API_MINOR 8, where OpenGL
  ES and WebGL2 windows had counted them from the bottom).
struct Light { sun: vec3f, shadow: f32, direct: vec3f,
  indirect: vec3f, emissive: vec3f, sun_direction: vec3f,
  sun_color: vec3f, ambient: vec3f, world: vec3f, normal: vec3f,
  uv: vec2f, base_color: vec4f, v0..v3: vec4f }   (since API_MINOR 9)
  sun the primary light's reflected light without its shadow and
  shadow that shadow (1 lit, 0 shadowed); direct the other lights'
  (their shadows applied); indirect ambient, hemisphere and
  environment light (ambient occlusion applied); emissive the
  surface's. The rest read-only: sun_direction toward the primary
  light, its color, the ambient color, and the fragment (normal the
  shading normal facing the viewer, the surface's base color and
  varyings). The primary light is the main light (see
  main_light_direction): its direction, color and shadow come apart
  here, and `shadow` already holds the light's `shadow.intensity`
  (three.js r185's LightShadow.intensity: mix(1, shadow, intensity)),
  so a partly shadowed main light needs no second, unshadowed fill
  light. Since API_MINOR 43 (`HOOK_ACCESS_MINOR`) Light also has
  `sun_diffuse: vec3f, sun_specular: vec3f` (before `ambient`): sun's
  diffuse part (the standard BRDF's (1 - metalness) × base, Lambert's
  and Phong's base, all of a toon surface's, times n·l and the light)
  and the rest, its specular highlight; read-only (sun is what is
  summed: `o.sun = l.sun_diffuse` drops the highlight, as URP's
  _SPECULARHIGHLIGHTS_OFF). The environment's reflection stays in
  `indirect`. v0..v3 are the surface hook's: what it writes to its
  Surface's v0..v3 (from the vertex varyings, or set there) the
  light hook reads (every minor), e.g. a mask kept apart from
  base_color's alpha.
struct Fog { color: vec3f, amount: f32, world: vec3f, depth: f32,
  coord: vec4f, camera: vec3f }               (since API_MINOR 9)
  color linear and amount 0 (none) to 1 (full): the scene's fog
  (black and 0 without one); fogged in display color as the scene's
  fog is (or in linear light before the post effects' tone mapping).
  Read-only: the fragment's world position, view depth and window
  position (rows from the top, for screen_uv, renderer.sceneDepth
  and renderer.sceneColor)
  and the camera's position.
fn model_matrix() -> mat4x4f       object to world, instance included
fn vertex_index() -> u32           (both vertex stage only)
fn view_projection() -> mat4x4f    world to clip (depth -1..1)
fn camera_position() -> vec3f
fn viewport_size() -> vec2f        in pixels
fn srgb_to_linear(c: vec3f) -> vec3f, fn linear_to_srgb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f
fn view_depth(world: vec3f) -> f32  distance along the camera's
                                   forward axis (since API_MINOR 8)
fn screen_uv(coord: vec4f) -> vec2f a window position as texture
                                   coordinates, 0..1 from the top
                                   left (since API_MINOR 8)
fn pass_kind() -> u32              the pass the hook runs in
                                   (since API_MINOR 26): PASS_MAIN
                                   (the lit pass), PASS_SHADOW (a
                                   shadow map's) or PASS_PREPASS
                                   (the depth or normal prepass)
fn is_shadow_pass() -> bool        pass_kind() == PASS_SHADOW: e.g.
                                   a hook that dithers its surface
                                   in view keeps its shadow solid
                                   (since API_MINOR 26; games below
                                   it may declare these names)
fn linear_fog() -> bool            whether this pass fogs in linear
                                   light (drawn through post
                                   buffers, tone mapped after) rather
                                   than in display color (an engine
                                   extension, since API_MINOR 40)
fn tone_mapped(c: vec3f) -> vec3f  a linear color tone mapped as
                                   this fragment's is where the pass
                                   draws straight (the renderer's
                                   tone mapping and exposure; c for
                                   a material not tone mapped; since
                                   API_MINOR 40)
fn fog_amount(world: vec3f) -> f32 the scene's fog at a world point as
                                   the pass fogs this material: 0
                                   (none, and for `fog` false) to 1;
                                   Fog's smoothstep from near to far
                                   or FogExp2's 1 - exp(-(density ×
                                   depth)²) of the view depth (an
                                   engine function every minor has;
                                   a fog hook's changes are not in it)
```

The game's clock, since API\_MINOR 49 (`HOOK_TIME_MINOR`; older games' programs neither have nor reserve these names: a hook calling one is refused as for any unknown name):

```text
fn frame_time() -> f32             seconds of game time since the
                                   first frame: frame().time in the
                                   frame drawn (what onUpdate and
                                   onRender read; paused while the
                                   game is suspended), as an f32, so
                                   a hook animated by it draws as one
                                   reading a uniform the game set to
                                   frame().time each frame, with no
                                   uniform to set. Not wrapped: an
                                   f32 holds it to about 1 ms after
                                   2.3 hours and 8 ms after a day; a
                                   game that needs finer steps in long
                                   sessions keeps a wrapped uniform
fn frame_delta() -> f32            seconds since the frame before
                                   (frame().delta; 0 on the first)
                                   Both the same in every hook (vertex,
                                   surface, light, fog and a
                                   ShaderMaterial's), both stages and
                                   every pass a hook runs in: the lit
                                   pass, shadow maps, the depth and
                                   normal prepasses, render targets.
                                   Motion vectors draw the mesh's own
                                   placement there (no hook runs), so a
                                   vertex hook's motion by time is not
                                   in them, as with any vertex hook.
                                   A caster marked static keeps its
                                   cached shadow (its hook's time is
                                   not watched, as uniforms are not)
```

The lights, since API\_MINOR 43 (`HOOK_ACCESS_MINOR`; older games' programs neither have nor reserve these names):

```text
struct PunctualLight { direction: vec3f, radiance: vec3f }
fn main_light_direction() -> vec3f toward the main light (Light's
                                   sun_direction): the scene's first
                                   directional light, shadow-casting
                                   or not
fn main_light_color() -> vec3f     its color × intensity (three.js's
                                   directLight.color; Light's
                                   sun_color); black without one
fn main_light_shadow(world: vec3f) -> f32

                                   lit, 0 shadowed): the cascade

                                   map type, radius, bias and
                                   intensity; PCF's noise and the
                                   receiver plane's slope this
                                   fragment's), with no normal offset
                                   (normalBias); 1 where it casts no
                                   shadow, outside its maps or
                                   without a main light, whatever the
                                   material's receiveShadow. At the
                                   fragment's own world point it is
                                   Light's `shadow` when normalBias
                                   is 0.
fn punctual_light_count() -> u32   the other lights' slots the pass
                                   takes (Light's `direct`:
                                   directional, point, spot and
                                   hemisphere lights after the main
                                   light, a slot each, and a
                                   LightProbe, two slots, in the
                                   scene's order: the 16 light slots'
                                   first, then the up to 64 clustered
                                   point and spot lights; at most 80,
                                   the engine's limit, past which
                                   lights are left out). The main
                                   light (the first directional
                                   light: the sun) is never among
                                   them, so slot 0 is the next light
                                   the scene holds. It is the same
                                   for every pixel of a draw (read
                                   from the pass's uniforms). A loop
                                   runs to a constant, so loop to 80u
                                   and leave at the count:
                                     let count = punctual_light_count();
                                     for (var i = 0u; i < 80u; i++) {
                                       if (i >= count) { break; }
                                       let p = punctual_light(i, l.world);
                                       ...
                                     }
